description.value: Participants viewed aversive photographs for 8 seconds under the close/reactivity instruction, imagining themselves close to the scene and allowing the evoked negative emotions; they then rated negative affect.

spans.text: On ‘close’ trials, participants were told to imagine standing close to the scene depicted in the photograph and to allow themselves to experience any emotions that the photograph evoked

description.value: Participants viewed aversive photographs for 8 seconds under the far/regulation instruction, imagining themselves farther from the scene and focusing on factual rather than emotional details; they then rated negative affect.

spans.text: On ‘far’ trials, participants were told to imagine standing further away from the scene and to focus more on the facts of the photograph than on its emotional details

instructions.value: Participants used close/reactivity or far/regulation strategies while viewing photographs. On close trials they imagined standing close to the scene and allowed themselves to experience the evoked emotions. On far trials they imagined standing farther away and focused on factual rather than emotional details. During passive re-presentation they viewed previously presented aversive images without regulating or rating their emotions.
